title: The Last and Lowliest
summary: The Ratkin tale of their place among the Changing Breeds.

claims.text: Ratkin tell that Gaia blessed the rat-folk last of all the Changing Breeds, the smallest and quietest, teaching the humans who loved rats to hide, find food anywhere and stay safe.
In their telling the Changing Breeds were once equals, the Bete, when the veil between flesh and spirit was thin as gossamer.

title: The Field of Nettles
summary: How the Ratkin remember the War of Rage.

claims.text: Ratkin remember the War of Rage as genocide: Garou hunted and herded wererats to be slaughtered, claiming the rat-folk carried disease.
The last Ratkin bards gathered at a sacred site called the Field of Nettles to compose a final tale of Garou betrayal, and died cursing the wolves with promises of plagues to come.
The survivors had already begun digging tunnels out of the physical world, and fled into the Umbra until the Garou believed them extinct.

title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe
summary: Great wererat families of the modern nights.

claims.text: Ratkin Tunnel Runners riddled the Shadow Curtain over Asia with boltholes, and when it fell in late 1998 the local wererats claimed the credit.
In Southeast Asia a criminal empire runs from a temple in Indonesia under the Giant Rat of Sumatra, a title handed down since the Victorian age.
The Horde roams the steppe and taiga from Mongolia to Siberia, meeting monthly to trade word of the supernatural; every member learns war and makes Pain Daggers.
Most Ratkin descend from brown rats, and only Plague Lords will admit to black-rat blood.
Europe's wererats answer to Madame DeFarge, who hides in the Paris sewers with a court dressed in the trappings of the French Revolution.

title: Rat Kings and Nests
summary: How a Ratkin colony is ruled.

claims.text: A Rat King rules a Ratkin nest and needs the backing of the eldest wererat of each aspect, often won by bargains, before taking the throne.
A senior Shadow Seer crowns the king in a formal rite that binds the ruler to the domain and lets the king watch it through the eyes of local rat-spirits.
Knife-Skulkers have a rite that names a killer of their pack or Rat King, which is one reason elders hire wererats just passing through for assassinations.
